question: How do I track my menstrual cycle
alternate_questions: How to keep track of menstruation
answer: You can track your cycle by marking the first day of your period each month. Count from day 1 of one period to day 1 of the next to determine cycle length. Note symptoms like cramps, mood changes, cervical mucus, and basal body temperature. Apps like Velora make this easy, but you can also use a calendar or journal. Tracking helps you understand your body and predict your next period.

question: What is basal body temperature tracking
answer: Basal body temperature (BBT) tracking involves taking your temperature first thing every morning before getting out of bed. Your temperature typically rises 0.5-1°F after ovulation due to progesterone. By charting this daily, you can identify when you've ovulated. It requires consistency and is best used to confirm ovulation rather than predict it. Special BBT thermometers are more accurate than regular ones.

question: How do I track cervical mucus
alternate_questions: What does cervical mucus look like
answer: To track cervical mucus, check your discharge daily by observing toilet paper after wiping or using clean fingers. During your fertile window, mucus becomes clear, stretchy, and similar to egg whites. After ovulation, it becomes thicker and cloudier. This method, also called the Billings method, helps identify your fertile days. Avoid checking during or right after sex, as semen can be mistaken for mucus.

question: What is the calendar method
answer: The calendar method involves tracking your cycle length over several months to predict fertile days. For a 28-day cycle, days 10-17 are typically considered fertile. You avoid unprotected sex during these days if preventing pregnancy. This method is less reliable than others because cycle length can vary. It's best combined with other fertility awareness methods and is not recommended for cycles shorter than 26 or longer than 32 days.

question: What are ovulation predictor kits
answer: Ovulation predictor kits (OPKs) detect the luteinizing hormone (LH) surge that occurs 24-36 hours before ovulation. You pee on a test strip or stick, similar to a pregnancy test. A positive result means you'll likely ovulate soon. OPKs are helpful for timing intercourse when trying to conceive. Test between 10am and 8pm, as LH surges often happen in the morning and show up in urine later.

question: How accurate are period tracking apps
answer: Period tracking apps are generally accurate for people with regular cycles, often predicting within 1-2 days. However, they rely on past data and algorithms, so irregular cycles, stress, illness, or lifestyle changes can affect accuracy. No app is 100% accurate, especially for contraception. Always use backup protection if avoiding pregnancy. The more data you input over time, the more accurate predictions become.

The key is consistency, mark the first day of every period and note any symptoms or changes.

question: What is fertility awareness method
answer: Fertility Awareness Method (FAM) involves tracking multiple signs to identify fertile and infertile days. It combines basal body temperature, cervical mucus observation, and calendar calculations. When practiced correctly, it can be 76-88% effective for contraception or helpful for conception. It requires daily commitment, training, and abstinence or barrier methods during fertile days. It's not recommended for those with irregular cycles.

question: How do I know if my cycle is regular
alternate_questions: How to tell if periods are regular
answer: A regular cycle typically varies by no more than 7-9 days from month to month. For example, if one cycle is 28 days and the next is 30 days, that's regular. If your cycle length jumps from 24 days to 35 days regularly, that may be considered irregular. Track for at least 3-6 months to determine your pattern. Some variation is normal, especially with stress, travel, or illness.

question: How do I track ovulation naturally
answer: Natural ovulation tracking involves observing: 1) Cervical mucus changes (egg-white consistency when fertile). 2) Cervical position (soft, high, open when fertile). 3) Basal body temperature rise after ovulation. 4) Mild pelvic pain (mittelschmerz). 5) Increased libido. 6) Breast tenderness. 7) Bloating. These signs combined give a good picture of your fertile window without buying tests.

question: What is a cycle day
answer: Cycle Day 1 is the first day of full menstrual bleeding (not spotting). You count forward from there. So if your period starts on Monday, Monday is CD1, Tuesday is CD2, and so on until your next period starts. The day before your next period is your last cycle day. A typical 28-day cycle has CD1 through CD28. This standardized counting helps healthcare providers and tracking apps communicate clearly about where you are in your cycle.

question: How do I track PMS symptoms
answer: Track PMS symptoms by logging physical and emotional changes in the 1-2 weeks before your period. Common symptoms include mood swings, irritability, bloating, breast tenderness, fatigue, cravings, headaches, and acne. Rate severity daily. After 2-3 months, patterns will emerge. This helps distinguish normal PMS from PMDD (which is more severe) and allows you to prepare coping strategies or seek treatment.

question: What is a luteal phase defect
answer: A luteal phase defect occurs when the luteal phase is shorter than 10 days or when progesterone levels are insufficient to maintain the uterine lining. This can make it difficult to conceive or maintain early pregnancy because the lining breaks down too early. It's diagnosed through blood tests, endometrial biopsy, or ultrasound. Treatment may include progesterone supplements or fertility medications.

question: How do I track my fertile window
answer: Your fertile window includes the 5 days before ovulation and ovulation day itself, since sperm can survive up to 5 days. Track by: 1) Counting back 14 days from your expected period in a 28-day cycle. 2) Using OPKs to detect LH surge. 3) Observing egg-white cervical mucus. 4) Monitoring basal body temperature rise. 5) Using fertility apps that combine these methods. Track for several months to identify your personal pattern.

question: What is cycle syncing
answer: Cycle syncing involves adjusting your diet, exercise, work, and social activities to match your menstrual cycle phases. For example: Menstruation - rest and gentle movement. Follicular - try new things and social activities. Ovulatory - high-intensity workouts and important meetings. Luteal - focus on organization and self-care. While popular, scientific evidence is limited. It can help some people feel more in tune with their bodies.
